To dive deeper, it helps to distinguish between two prominent entities in hip-hop under this phonetic name: K Deezy, the influential underground Detroit rap veteran, and KADEEZY, the contemporary independent hip-hop producer and digital artist.
1. K Deezy (Detroit Rap Legend)
If you are looking for classic, hard-hitting mid-2000s street rap, you are likely thinking of K-Doe aka K Deezy. He is a foundational member of the legendary Detroit rap collective Street Lord'z. 
The Breakthrough: His 2005 breakthrough record, "In My Hood," became a defining anthem for Detroit hip-hop. Originally written spontaneously in the shower following an argument, the song was initially rejected by local radio stations for being too aggressive. However, regional demand forced it onto the airwaves, making it a major unified street anthem across different city neighborhoods. 
Classic Albums: His definitive solo album, Stuck In My Ways (2005), features high-profile collaborations with Detroit staple Royce Da 5'9", Cash Money Records veteran B.G., and the Street Lord'z. 

YouTube
Signature Sound: Known for high-energy, raw lyricism layered over heavy, chopped-and-screwed Midwestern beats produced by local collaborators like Kid. 

YouTube

2. KADEEZY (Modern Independent Artist)
If you are looking for abstract, multi-genre soundscapes, you are thinking of the modern independent creator KADEEZY (often stylized in all caps).
The Style: This project leans heavily into motivational, self-reflective, and introspective rap blended with spacey electronic elements and digital art.
The Catalog: Releases include concept-driven projects like Me Vs The Universe, Only Mine To Claim, and the track "The Dying Inside Run."
Distribution: Much of this work bridges the gap between underground audio streaming and open-access digital repositories (such as Zenodo) to showcase independent, self-produced media catalogs.
